title: Right unit constraint for normalized ringed tensor comparison on flat-term K-flat representatives
statement: In the setting of [lem-sf-ringed-forget-tensor-unit-representatives], [def-sf-ringed-forget-tensor-transposition-data] and [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], use the normalized unit isomorphism given by the explicit composite in the Lean declaration. Given hU, a total-tensor comparison chain and its summand formula, and a RepresentativeModel hμ as in the parent statement, for every flat-term K-flat complex P the right unit square displayed in the Lean declaration `ringed_forget_tensor_right_representatives` holds. The proof uses [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] for the exact-functor localization factor.

source.place: Tag 0FPT, with 06YU; unit verification in steps 2–3 of lem-sf-ringed-forget-tensor-coherence.

proof.text: The coefficient unit in degree zero has flat terms: its degree-zero term is the monoidal unit and its other terms are zero. The bounded-above flat criterion makes it K-flat. Apply hU to this unit and to P to obtain the K-flatness needed in the representative comparison.

Extract the two chain right unitors from cB.rightUnitor_model and cA.rightUnitor_model. Their local pure-tensor equations determine the restriction to the (n,0) summand: tensor the degree-zero single-complex identification with the identity and then apply the underived right unitor. This follows from the sheafification adjunction, pure-tensor extensionality and the sheaf right-unitor formula.

Let e be the composite from the image of the source unit complex to the target unit complex, using singleMapHomologicalComplex and the given underived unit. Prove the chain square by precomposing the inverse chain comparison and testing target totalization summands. Summands with second degree nonzero vanish, since additive U preserves the zero term. On (n,0), the summand hypothesis and the preceding unitor formulas reduce the square to tensor-comparison naturality and u.coherence.right_unit. The degree-zero component of e followed by the target single identification is U of the source single identification followed by the underived unit.

Use hmu at (P,unit complex), naturality of cA.tensorIso along e, and tensorIso_both to compare the two tensor models. Localize the chain square and use naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors. A categorical cancellation argument, using naturality of mu along cB.unitIso and right-unitor naturality along the localization factor of P, gives exactly the displayed equation with the normalized composite unit.

theorem ringed_forget_tensor_right_representatives
    (hU : ∀ P : CochainComplex (RingedTensorModules.{c, v, r} J R) ℤ,
      P.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients →
      (∀ p : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite.{c, v, max c v r, max c v r}
        (R := R) (P.X p)) →
      CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := R')
        ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ∧
      ∀ p : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite.{d, vd, max d vd s, max d vd s}
        (R := R') (U.obj (P.X p)))
    (chain : coefficientTotalTensor.{r, c, v} J R ⋙ U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ≅
      ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).prod (U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))) ⋙
        coefficientTotalTensor.{s, d, vd} J' R')
    (summand : ∀ (P Q : CochainComplex (RingedTensorModules.{c, v, r} J R) ℤ)
      (p q n : ℤ) (hpq : p + q = n),
      U.map (tensorSummand.{c, v, r} J R P Q p q n hpq) ≫ (chain.hom.app (P, Q)).f n =
        u.tensor.hom.app (P.X p, Q.X q) ≫
          tensorSummand.{d, vd, s} J' R' ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
            ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q) p q n hpq)
    (μ : SB.tensor ⋙ U.mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (U.mapDerivedCategory.prod U.mapDerivedCategory) ⋙ SA.tensor)
    (hμ : RepresentativeModel.{c, v, r, d, vd, s, wb, wa}
      J R J' R' U SB TB SA TA chain μ.hom)
    (P : CochainComplex (RingedTensorModules.{c, v, r} J R) ℤ)
    (hP : P.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients)
    (fP : ∀ p : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite.{c, v, max c v r, max c v r}
      (R := R) (P.X p)) :
    μ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P, SB.monoidal.tensorUnit) ≫
        SA.tensor.map
          (X := (U.mapDerivedCategory.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P),
            U.mapDerivedCategory.obj SB.monoidal.tensorUnit))
          (Y := (U.mapDerivedCategory.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P), SA.monoidal.tensorUnit))
          (𝟙 _, (U.mapDerivedCategory.mapIso cB.unitIso ≪≫
              U.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.app (ringedTensorUnitComplex.{c, v, r} J R) ≪≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso
                ((HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex U (.up ℤ) 0).app
                  (SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J
                    (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R))) ≪≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso
                ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) (0 : ℤ)).mapIso u.coherence.unit) ≪≫
              cA.unitIso.symm).hom) ≫
        (SA.monoidal.rightUnitor (U.mapDerivedCategory.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P))).hom =
      U.mapDerivedCategory.map (SB.monoidal.rightUnitor (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)).hom
